extracted.intended_audience: small businesses and their advocates submitting comments to federal agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for small businesses on preparing effective notice-and-comment letters to influence federal rulemaking. Covers how to read a proposed rule, structure a letter, make persuasive arguments, and meet procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully review proposed regulations in the Federal Register and identify areas with the most significant business impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus attention on the provisions that will affect your operations; read the proposed rule text and supporting materials so your comments address the agency's actual proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Clear and Concise
rubrics_metrics.description: State your purpose early in the letter and use plain language to ensure regulatory agencies understand your concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a clear statement of intent and avoid unnecessary jargon so reviewers can quickly grasp your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain Business Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete examples of operational effects, including supporting data, cost estimates, and industry benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify impacts where possible (costs, time, scale) and use real examples from your business to demonstrate practical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest specific, practical alternatives to problematic provisions and emphasize how changes benefit both business and consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose workable edits, regulatory alternatives, or implementation approaches rather than just criticizing; explain mutual benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a respectful, constructive tone and follow each agency's submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep comments professional and procedural requirements (format, submission method) in mind so the agency accepts and considers your input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction (letter structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify yourself, the rule name, your business relevance, and key concerns in the opening of the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place identification and relevance up front to establish standing and context for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body (letter structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe supported or opposed provisions with specific explanations and supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address particular regulatory provisions, state whether you support or oppose them, and back each position with evidence or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion (letter structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize main points and thank the agency in closing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterate key requests or recommendations succinctly to leave a clear takeaway for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine a clear claim, supporting data (quantified impact), and an explanation of why the evidence matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure each argument around these three elements so agency staff can follow the logic and relevance of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific with details and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific details and data when describing impacts and arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete figures, timeframes, and operational descriptions make your comment more persuasive than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite sources clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear citations for data and benchmarks used to support your claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the origin of statistics, studies, or industry standards so reviewers can verify and rely on your evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish credibility through relevant experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate relevant business experience or expertise to support your perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why your business or role gives you informed insight into the issue (e.g., years in operation, customer base, industry role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible language and professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in accessible language while maintaining a professional tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dense legalese or overly technical phrasing that could obscure your point; be respectful and constructive in wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the letter for clarity, accuracy, and errors before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful proofreading improves credibility and reduces the chance your point is misunderstood or dismissed due to mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments before the deadline (typically 30-60 days) to allow adequate agency review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing ensures your comment will be considered; check the Federal Register notice for exact deadlines and submit accordingly.
